q: This ode again was written neither for a Nemean nor for any other athletic victory, but for the [Greek: eisitaeria] or initiatory ceremonies at the election of a new [Greek: prytanis] of Tenedos.

s: initiatory ceremonies mark election of the Prytanis (at the accession of a new Prytanis)
q: This ode again was written neither for a Nemean nor for any other athletic victory, but for the [Greek: eisitaeria] or initiatory ceremonies at the election of a new [Greek: prytanis] of Tenedos.

s: Hestia is a Daughter of Rhea
q: Daughter of Rhea, who hast in thy keeping the city halls[1], O Hestia

s: Hestia is sister of Zeus (highest Zeus)
q: O Hestia! sister of highest Zeus and of Hera sharer of his throne

s: Hestia shares throne with Hera
q: O Hestia! sister of highest Zeus and of Hera sharer of his throne

s: Hestia keeps Prytaneion (the city halls)
q: The sacred fire of the state, over which Hestia watched, was kept in the Prytaneion.

s: Hestia's sanctuary receives Aristagoras of Tenedos (with good-will)
q: with good-will welcome Aristagoras to thy sanctuary

s: Hestia's sanctuary has fellows who draw near Senate of Tenedos (with good-will)
q: with good-will also his fellows[2] who draw nigh to thy glorious sceptre

s: rites of Zeus honor Zeus (at tables and as rites of hospitality)
q: and at their tables never-failing are celebrated the rites of Zeus, the stranger's friend.

s: drink-offerings honor Hestia (performed many times before the other gods)
q: by drink-offerings glorifying thee many times before the other gods

s: burnt sacrifice honors Hestia (performed many times)
q: and many times by the savour of burnt sacrifice

s: Aristagoras's clan has won sixteen neighboring athletic victories (in wrestling and pankration)
q: Now among the neighbouring peoples sixteen illustrious victories have crowned Aristagoras and his famous clan in the wrestling-match and in the pankration of weighty honour.

s: Peisander is an ancestor of Aristagoras of Tenedos (head of Aristagoras's clan)
q: Ancestor of Aristagoras and head of his clan.

s: Aiolians are brought to Tenedos (in bronze mail, with Orestes)
q: for from Amyklai he came[5] with Orestes, bringing hither an army of Aiolians in bronze mail

s: Aristagoras of Tenedos has father Arkesilas
q: Blessed among men I count his father Arkesilas, and himself for his splendid body and his heritage of a dauntless heart.

s: wealth can be possessed by human beings (along with superior beauty and athletic strength)
q: But if any man shall possess wealth, and withal surpass his fellows in comely form, and in games have shown his strength to be the best

s: human destiny leads on race of mortals (through successive generations)
q: Thus also doth destiny lead on the race of mortals.

s: Aristagoras of Tenedos has attribute splendid body
q: Blessed among men I count his father Arkesilas, and himself for his splendid body and his heritage of a dauntless heart.

s: Aristagoras of Tenedos has attribute dauntless heart (by heritage)
q: Blessed among men I count his father Arkesilas, and himself for his splendid body and his heritage of a dauntless heart.

s: Aristagoras of Tenedos belongs to Aristagoras's clan (famous clan)
q: Now among the neighbouring peoples sixteen illustrious victories have crowned Aristagoras and his famous clan in the wrestling-match and in the pankration of weighty honour.

s: Aristagoras of Tenedos has won sixteen neighboring athletic victories (among neighbouring peoples)
q: Now among the neighbouring peoples sixteen illustrious victories have crowned Aristagoras and his famous clan in the wrestling-match and in the pankration of weighty honour.

s: Aristagoras of Tenedos competes in wrestling (among neighbouring peoples)
q: Now among the neighbouring peoples sixteen illustrious victories have crowned Aristagoras and his famous clan in the wrestling-match and in the pankration of weighty honour.

s: Pindar's ode is for Hieron of Syracuse (winner in the horse-race)
q: FOR HIERON OF SYRACUSE, WINNER IN THE HORSE-RACE.

s: Hieron of Syracuse is king of Syracusans (as their king)
q: and brought victory to his master, the Syracusans' king, who delighteth in horses.

s: Hieron of Syracuse wields sceptre of justice (in Sicily)
q: for he wieldeth the sceptre of justice in Sicily of many flocks

s: Hieron of Syracuse possesses excellence (in many kinds)
q: culling the choice fruits of all kinds of excellence

s: Dorian lute accompanies Pindar's ode (in celebrating Pherenikos' victory)
q: Take from the peg the Dorian lute, if in any wise the glory of Pherenikos[2] at Pisa hath swayed thy soul unto glad thoughts

s: Pherenikos wins horse-race (at Pisa)
q: the glory of Pherenikos[2] at Pisa hath swayed thy soul unto glad thoughts, when by the banks of Alpheos he ran, and gave his body ungoaded in the course

s: Pherenikos belongs to Hieron of Syracuse (as his winning horse)
q: and brought victory to his master, the Syracusans' king, who delighteth in horses.

s: Pisa is colony of Lydian Pelops' colony (as the site of the race)
q: Bright is his fame in Lydian Pelops' colony

s: Pelops is loved by Poseidon (as the founder of the Olympic games)
q: whose founder mighty earth-enfolding Poseidon loved

s: Poseidon has the Bright Trident
q: then did he of the Bright Trident

s: Pindar's ode is about Olympic games (especially their preeminence among games)
q: This ode seems to owe its position at the head of Pindar's extant works to Aristophanes the grammarian, who placed it there on account of its being specially occupied with the glorification of the Olympic games in comparison with others

s: Pelops is created by Klotho (from a vessel of purifying, with an ivory shoulder)
q: from the vessel of purifying[4] Klotho took him with the bright ivory furnishment of his shoulder

s: Tantalos is father of Pelops
q: Of thee, son of Tantalos

s: Tantalos hosts gods (at his beloved Sipylos)
q: when thy father had bidden thee to that most seemly feast at his beloved Sipylos, repaying to the gods their banquet

s: Poseidon abducts Pelops (to Zeus's house in Olympus)
q: did he of the Bright Trident[6], his heart vanquished by love, snatch thee and bear thee behind his golden steeds to the house of august Zeus in the highest

s: Pelops' abduction is carried to Poseidon (behind his golden steeds)
q: snatch thee and bear thee behind his golden steeds to the house of august Zeus in the highest

s: Ganymede comes to Zeus (on a similar errand after Pelops's abduction)
q: whither again on a like errand came Ganymede in the after time.

s: Tantalos is honored by gods (as one who had honor of the guardians of Olympus)
q: Now if any man ever had honour of the guardians of Olympus, Tantalos was that man

s: Tantalos is punished by gods (for stealing nectar and ambrosia and giving them to mortals)
q: This hopeless life of endless misery he endureth with other three[7], for that he stole from the immortals and gave to his fellows at a feast the nectar and ambrosia

s: Pindar's ode is about Pelops (as founder of the games)
q: and with the story of Pelops, who was their founder.

s: Tantalos possesses nectar and ambrosia (which he stole from the immortals and gave to mortals)
q: he stole from the immortals and gave to his fellows at a feast the nectar and ambrosia

s: Pelops is returned to short-lived race of men (by the immortals)
q: Therefore also the immortals sent back again his son to be once more counted with the short-lived race of men.

s: Pelops marries Hippodameia (after reaching youth)
q: took counsel with himself speedily to take to him for his wife the noble Hippodameia from her Pisan father's hand.

s: Pelops and Hippodameia's marriage is between Pelops (and Hippodameia)
q: to take to him for his wife the noble Hippodameia

s: Hippodameia is daughter of Oinomaos (the Pisan father)
q: the noble Hippodameia from her Pisan father's hand

s: Oinomaos has killed thirteen lovers (before agreeing to give Hippodameia in marriage)
q: Thirteen lovers already hath Oinomaos slain, and still delayeth to give his daughter in marriage.

s: Poseidon gives golden car (to Pelops for the contest against Oinomaos)
q: for the god made him a glorious gift of a golden car and winged untiring steeds

s: Poseidon gives winged untiring steeds (to Pelops for the contest against Oinomaos)
q: for the god made him a glorious gift of a golden car and winged untiring steeds

s: Pelops overcomes Oinomaos (in the race for Hippodameia)
q: so he overcame Oinomaos and won the maiden for his bride.

s: Hieron of Syracuse wins horse-race (at Olympia)
q: Hieron won this race B.C. 472, while at the height of his power at Syracuse.

s: Pelops has six sons of Pelops (with Hippodameia)
q: And he begat six sons, chieftains, whose thoughts were ever of brave deeds

s: Pelops has Pelops' tomb (beside the Alpheos stream)
q: and now hath he part in honour of blood-offerings in his grave beside Alpheos' stream, and hath a frequented tomb

s: Olympic chariot race has courses called after Olympic games (at the Olympian games)
q: from afar off he beholdeth the glory of the Olympian games in the courses called of Pelops

s: Olympic games are founded by Pelops (according to the ode's tradition)
q: with the story of Pelops, who was their founder.

s: Pindar's ode uses Aeolian strain (to crown Hieron)
q: My part it is to crown Hieron with an equestrian strain in Aeolian mood

s: Muse has strongest-wingëd dart (still in store for Hieron's future glory)
q: Her strongest-wingëd dart my Muse hath yet in store.

s: Pindar is a poet (a friend of winners in the games)
q: and mine to be the friend of winners in the games, winning honour for my art among Hellenes everywhere.

s: Aristophanes the grammarian places Pindar's ode (at the head of Pindar's extant works)
q: This ode seems to owe its position at the head of Pindar's extant works to Aristophanes the grammarian, who placed it there

s: Olympic games are greatest games (among all games)
q: neither shall we find any games greater than the Olympic

s: Olympic games inspire glorious hymn (through their renown)
q: for hence cometh the glorious hymn

s: Pindar is a poet
q: Pindar was engaged at the time to write an ode in honour of the Delian Apollo to be sung at Keos

s: Thebes is described as golden shield (in apostrophe)
q: O mother, Thebe of the golden shield

s: Thebes is native state of Pindar
q: put this off in order first to write the present ode in honour of a victory won for his own native state of Thebes

s: Thebes is home of people of Kadmos
q: For six crowns hath Isthmos given from her games to the people of Kadmos, a fair glory of triumph for my country

s: Thebes is land of birth of Heracles (through Alkmene)
q: for the land wherein Alkmene bare her dauntless son

s: Delos is a rocky island (sacred to Apollo)
q: May rocky Delos, whereto I am vowed, be not therefore wroth with me.

s: Delos is associated with Apollo (as the Apollonian island)
q: Give place O Apollonian isle

s: Isthmos is a sea-prisoning cliffs
q: and therewithal this other for the sea-prisoning cliffs of Isthmos.

s: Isthmos gives crowns to people of Kadmos (six crowns from its games)
q: For six crowns hath Isthmos given from her games to the people of Kadmos

s: Isthmian Games award crowns people of Kadmos (six crowns)
q: For six crowns hath Isthmos given from her games to the people of Kadmos

s: Pindar writes ode for Herodotos of Thebes (in honour of his chariot victory)
q: But I for Herodotos' praise am fain to do honour unto his four-horsed car

s: chariot race is won by Herodotos of Thebes
q: FOR HERODOTOS OF THEBES. WINNER IN THE CHARIOT-RACE.

s: Herodotos' four-horsed car is honoured by Pindar (in song)
q: But I for Herodotos' praise am fain to do honour unto his four-horsed car

s: Alkmene is mother of Heracles
q: for the land wherein Alkmene bare her dauntless son

s: Kastor is a heroic charioteer (among the mightiest)
q: For these Kastor and Iolaos were of all heroes the mightiest charioteers

s: Kastor belongs to Lakedaimon (as its hero)
q: the one to Lakedaimon

s: Kastor has father Tyndareus
q: the son of Tyndareus inhabiting the upland dwelling-place of Therapna

s: Iolaos belongs to Thebes (born there)
q: the other born to Thebes

s: Asopodoros is driven ashore on a wrecked ship
q: when he drave ashore on a wrecked ship, harboured him amid his dismal hap

s: Orchomenos harbours Asopodoros (after a shipwreck)
q: his new country Orchomenos, which, when he drave ashore on a wrecked ship, harboured him amid his dismal hap

s: Poseidon is a earth-shaking son of Kronos (worshipped as a benefactor)
q: beseemeth to requite the earth-shaking son of Kronos, who is also neighbour unto us, and to sound his praise as our well-doer

s: Poseidon is associated with Isthmos (as its deity and neighbour)
q: Us it beseemeth to requite the earth-shaking son of Kronos, who is also neighbour unto us

s: Kronos is father of Poseidon
q: the earth-shaking son of Kronos

s: Hermes gives prizes to Herodotos of Thebes (through his horses)
q: that Hermes lord of games hath given to Herodotos by his horses

s: Pytho is a place of victory wreaths (whose wreaths Herodotos may win again)
q: yet again with wreaths from Pytho

s: Pindar composes Iolaic song (for Herodotos' victory)
q: and to marry to the strain of Kastoreian or Iolaic song the fame that he hath earned

s: Olympic games provide wreaths Herodotos of Thebes (through Alpheos)
q: choice wreaths from Alpheos from the Olympian games

s: Mortal excellence is a desire (when wholly pursued with wealth and toil)
q: If a man's desire be wholly after valour, and he give thereto both wealth and toil

s: glory is a reward (the highest reward for victory in games or war)
q: but whoso in the games or in war hath won delightful fame, receiveth the highest of rewards in fair words of citizens and of strangers.

s: Herodotos of Thebes is a chariot-race winner
q: FOR HERODOTOS OF THEBES. WINNER IN THE CHARIOT-RACE.

s: Herodotos of Thebes drives Herodotos' four-horsed car (with his own hands and without assistance)
q: handling his reins in his own and no helping hand

s: Herodotos of Thebes has father Asopodoros
q: the story of his father Asopodoros' fate
